newsitem.title: cambodia: Cambodian royalist dissident plans party congress.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian royalist dissident plans party congress.

text.p: A Cambodian royalist dissident said on Wednesday he hoped to hold his own party congress before the end of May in what would be an unprecedented challenge to co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Toan Chhay, governor of the northwest province of Siem Reap, told a news conference he hoped to hold a congress with 100 to 150 supporters, but that security concerns would make it "very difficult".
Toan Chhay has emerged as the nominal leader of a breakaway group of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party, which split with the prince last week.
The dissident group initially claimed the support of 12 FUNCINPEC parliamentarians, but eight have since announced they had rejoined the royalist party.
Toan Chhay on Wednesday appeared with several of his fellow dissidents, including Minister of State Ung Phan, who led the initial break with FUNCINPEC, questioning the leadership of Ranariddh.
Both men, along with two other senior provincial officials and a military commander, have been ejected from the party.

Toan Chhay told reporters his faction of FUNCINPEC would seek to reform the party platform and guidelines, strengthen the monarchy and attempt to improve relations between FUNCINPEC and co-Premier Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party (CPP).
"It's not the government that has the power. The party has the power. This I don't want to accept and I will not accept," he said in criticism of the country's factional political leadership.

Ranariddh has shared power with Hun Sen in an uneasy coalition formed after U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993. On Wednesday he said verbal sparring between the two sides only made the political situation worse.

"If we continue the war of words...it could lead to a massacre again, but who will be the victims of the massacres? The victims are never the leaders, because the leaders always have bodyguards escorting them," he said in a radio broadcast.

Relations between the two leaders are at an all-time low following last month's grenade attack on an opposition rally which killed almost 20 people and accusations by Ranariddh that Hun Sen orchestrated the split in FUNCINPEC.
